constraints: The netlist is a flat, synthesized gate-level Verilog file.
The design contains a finite state machine implemented with standard cells and D-type flip-flops.
The analysis must be performed on the provided netlist without modification.
expected_outputs: A valid trojan_report.json file in the submission directory.
The report must contain a list of suspect nodes with associated labels.
The report must be parseable JSON conforming to the specified schema.

functional_requirements.requirement: The submitted trojan_report.json file must be syntactically valid JSON and parseable by a standard JSON parser.
The report must contain the top-level key "suspect_nodes" with a value that is an array.
Each element in the "suspect_nodes" array must be an object containing exactly two keys, "node_name" and "role", both with string values.

interface: The participant must produce a single file named trojan_report.json inside the submission/ directory. The file must be valid JSON with the following structure: an object containing a key "suspect_nodes" which maps to an array of objects. Each object in the array must have two string fields: "node_name" (the exact hierarchical name of a net or cell instance from the netlist) and "role" (a short label describing its suspected function, e.g., "trigger_logic", "payload_gate", "state_register").
objective: Analyze the provided gate-level netlist and identify any suspicious sequential logic structures and their downstream effects. Submit a report listing all suspect nodes and their roles.
response_format: A JSON file named trojan_report.json with the following schema: {"suspect_nodes": [{"node_name": "string", "role": "string"}]}
